items.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: guys were starting to write Bach type fugues and calling it jazz

ctx.x: They’ve got a music word to use and make it cool at the same time.

Yeah. And then guys were starting to write Bach type fugues and calling it jazz, just because it was counterpuntal and it got to be ridiculous. The thing that disturbed me about that scene the most was they’d decide to record a guy, and they’d hire an outside arranger to write the music. The arranger brings the music in to the date and that’s the first time that the artist has seen the music. You know it has nothing to do with him except there are spots in it for him to play. Now most of the guys that record do…
Right. Because otherwise it’s a pretty contrived situation, they’re trying to second-guess what’s going to sell.
